title: Cases filed per court, measured from the published case files
description: CSM's Anexa 1 prints Volum and Cauze soluţionate for each court. Volum is the volume of activity — stock carried in plus everything filed during the year — so neither column is the count of new cases, and that count is published nowhere. It is what the case files give directly, because every dosar carries a registration date. This document holds it, beside CSM's volume for context. What the schema is built to prevent is the reading that the ratio between them audits the published figure: filings are a component of volume, not a rival estimate of it, so the ratio is a lower bound on how much of a court's year is new work and never a verdict on CSM's arithmetic.

an.description: Calendar year of registration being counted, and the CSM edition it is set against.

acoperire.description: Which courts joined and which did not. Reported rather than dropped: a court missing from one side is a fact about the two vocabularies, and silently excluding it would make the national totals quietly wrong.

acoperireDinRaport.description: True when the crawled set came from the coverage report, which lists every court visited. False when it was inferred from the parquet, which cannot show a court that returned nothing — so the crawled set is then short by exactly the silent courts.

doarInCsm.description: Expected members are the Înalta Curte, which is not on the portal, and the military courts the annex carries but the enum does not.

doarInPortal.description: Expected members are the suspended judecătorii, which exist in law and in the enum but not in the annex.

intrate.description: Cases registered at this court in the compared year, counted from the case files. A floor: cases already archived are no longer visible.

intratePerVolum.description: Lower bound on the share of the court's year that is new work rather than inherited stock. Not a check on CSM's figure.

divergentaCota.description: cotaIntrate minus cotaVolum. Positive means the court files a larger share of the national total than its share of published volume. More robust than the levels either side of it, because a survivorship factor that applies broadly cancels in a ratio of shares.
